BUYER TOOLS

Compare before
you buy.

The Fabrication Intelligence Price Finder is a free browser extension for Chrome and Edge. Open any product page, say a keyboard on one shop, click the button, and it shows that same product on other Australian shops with prices, lowest first, so you can find it cheaper before you buy.

Download the extension, freeHow to install it

Version 0.3.0, small zip, no account needed

  2. Use it on any product

Install in 3 steps

  1. Download and unzip. Use the button above, then unzip the file somewhere you will keep it. Do not delete the folder, the browser reads it from there.
  2. Open your extensions page. In Chrome go to chrome://extensions, in Edge go to edge://extensions. Turn on Developer mode (a switch at the top or side of the page).
  3. Load it. Choose Load unpacked and pick the unzipped folder. Then open the puzzle-piece menu in your toolbar and pin Fabrication Intelligence Price Finder so it is one click away.

It is not in the Chrome Web Store or Edge Add-ons yet, which is why it installs this way. We plan to submit it once it has had real use.

Use it on any product

  1. Find a product. Open a product page on any shop: a keyboard, a kettle, a handle, anything you are about to buy.
  2. Click the FABINT icon. It reads the product name, brand and model number shown on that page, only when you click, and shows what it is searching for.
  3. Compare. It lists shops that sell the same product with their prices, lowest first, from Google Shopping listings. Below that are quick links to search Google Shopping, PriceSpy, eBay Australia, Amazon Australia and Kogan yourself. For hardware such as handles, knobs and hinges it also lists similar Fabrication Intelligence products with our starting price.
  4. Check and buy. Click a shop to open its page, check it is the same model, size and colour, add delivery to each price, then buy where it is cheapest. You can also type what you want into the search box.

Download the extension, free

What it reads and what leaves your browser

  • It reads the page only when you click the button (the activeTab permission). It cannot see your other tabs or your browsing history.
  • The page itself is never sent anywhere. Its address, your other tabs and your browsing are never sent either.
  • Only the product name goes to our server, which asks a price search service (SearchApi) for Google Shopping listings in Australia. We keep the search in memory for up to a day to save lookups, and we do not store who asked. A shop only sees the product name when you click its link.
  • The other network request downloads our public product list from fabricationintelligence.com, which is saved on your device for one hour (the storage permission).
  • It has no accounts, no tracking and no adverts.

Honest limits

  • Prices come from Google Shopping listings and can be out of date or differ at checkout. The shop's own page is the final word, and delivery is not included.
  • The service has a daily lookup limit while it is free. When it is used up or switched off, the extension still shows the shop links.
  • Search results can include similar products, not identical ones. Check model, size, colour and pack quantity, and add delivery, before you buy.
  • Fabrication Intelligence matches only appear for hardware, and our prices are starting prices that depend on size and finish.
  • It works best on pages that publish standard product data, and uses the page title when they do not. When it cannot read a page, use the search box.
